data.narrative:
Pale Blue, a Series A space & aerospace company founded by Jun Asakawa and Yuichi Nakagawa, has raised $7.5M in equity plus $27M in grant funding. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three standard triangulation methods, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach was excluded due to insufficient same-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector—while 14 sector peers exist, fewer than 3 met narrow filters for stage and valuation proximity. Public-comp anchoring using a 27.4x median P/S multiple across the 5 public tickers was inapplicable absent disclosed revenue for the target. Stage-progression, using the $8M total-raised proxy as a base, applies a standard 2.0x Series A–to–next-stage multiplier, yielding $15M.

The single-method constraint significantly limits confidence. The triangulated range of $13M–$17M (median $15M) reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression result, serving as a directional anchor rather than a robust valuation. Key uncertainties include the grant funding's impact on future equity requirements and dilution, patent portfolio depth, and the target's revenue trajectory relative to scaled peers. A narrower range would require either same-stage private comparables or disclosed financial metrics.
